paragraphs.sourceText: By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it 26 too late to start?
paragraphs.translationZh: 到目前为止，人们普遍认为，对于长期保持这种习惯的人来说，定期锻炼可以带来多种健康益处。但现在开始会不会太晚了？

paragraphs.sourceText: New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early 27 which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a 28 of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of 29 diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 新的研究观察了那些在 40 多岁之后将运动水平提高到超过年轻时水平的人，这些人的早期死亡风险有所下降，这与终生坚持锻炼的人相似。与不锻炼的人相比，这一数字下降了 32% 至 35%。那些中年开始锻炼的人，心脏病和癌症等慢性病的发病率也有所降低，这与坚持锻炼的人相似。

paragraphs.sourceText: So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study 30 that some might interpret the study’s findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not 31 . These real health benefits include better 32 functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is 33 important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those 34 later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or 35 , and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，为什么要费心一生坚持锻炼呢？该研究的作者承认，有些人可能会将研究结果解读为他们可以推迟开始锻炼计划，但这将是一个错误。保持持续活跃还有其他我们不应忽视的好处，无论是精神上还是身体上。这些真正的健康益处包括更好的认知功能和降低体重增加的风险。鉴于全球肥胖流行，后者尤为重要。此外，专家断言，越早开始越好，因为如果你在年轻时养成锻炼的习惯，你就更有可能在以后的生活中保持这些模式。因此，人们从儿童或青少年时期开始锻炼是理想的选择，而且无论年龄大小，始终保持积极的生活方式都是有好处的。然而，这项研究确实表明，如果您一直不运动，那么如果您在 40 多岁和 50 多岁时开始运动，您仍然可以受益。

paragraphs.sourceText: Restaurants Are Now Employing Robots — Should Chefs Be Worried?
paragraphs.translationZh: 餐厅现在正在使用机器人——厨师应该担心吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. But you won’t hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 像大多数厨师一样，Flippy 不惧怕艰苦的工作。自去年夏天以来，这意味着在加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的 Caliburger 进行上午 11 点到晚上 7 点的轮班，以及在洛杉矶道奇体育场的 Chick-N-Tots 进行短期任务。这些都是长时间的重复性工作，老板要求绝对的一致性。但事实上，你不会听到 Flippy 抱怨或说什么。 Flippy 是一个机器人——一个与云连接的机械臂，配有 3D 眼睛热扫描仪——每小时可以翻转汉堡或煎炸 80 篮食物，监控食物，甚至在事后清理。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: “A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers.” Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. And Flippy is not alone. Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) Flippy 由 Cali Group 旗下的 Miso Robotics 创建，其首席执行官 John Miller 将其描述为：“一家碰巧销售芝士汉堡的科技公司。” Cali 创造了新机器，并在世界各地的 Caliburger 餐厅进行路测，今年将部署 Flippy。 Flippy 并不孤单。同样在加利福尼亚州，Bear Robotics 开发了一款自动引导机器人 Penny，迄今为止已为 40,000 名食客提供服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers “an immediate return”, says Bear Robotics’ chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 十年前，机器人厨师和服务员纯粹是科幻小说。如今，它们已成为现实，而且其价格也使其成为一项合理的投资。 Bear Robotics 首席运营官胡安·伊格罗斯 (Juan Higueros) 表示，从 5 月份开始，Penny 将以订阅方式发货，并提供“立即回报”。据报道，Flippy 的售价为 60,000 至 100,000 美元。完全自动化的汉堡餐厅以最少的人为监督进行管理——顾客在屏幕上点餐、电子支付、吃由机器人烹饪和交付的食物——现在已经成为可能。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald’s is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）技术存在；它只需要以成本效益高且食客认可的方式组合在一起。在一个热衷于削减劳动力成本和增加利润的行业中，进一步的自动化似乎是不可避免的。在加利福尼亚州 Kang Nam Tofu House 进行了为期 8 个月的测试后，Bear Robotics 认为 Penny 推动了销售额增长 28%。与此同时，在美国的试验中，麦当劳目前在其 1,300 家英国餐厅安装的自助点餐屏幕据称使订单价值增长了 30%。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called “upsells” (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you — factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 个性化被视为这项技术吸引力的关键，此外它还能够可靠地向顾客推销所谓的“追加销售”（餐食优惠、额外服务、大杯饮料）。很快，当您登录餐厅应用程序时，它将能够使用您的数据和购买历史记录向您推荐菜肴 - 考虑到从天气到您的心情（如果您在可以读取您的面部表情的屏幕上点餐）的所有因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) “Right now people compromise on choice. We’re presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. You love spicy food and chicken? Here’s the dish people like you mostly order,” says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. “For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) “现在人们在选择上妥协了。我们看到的是一份通用的菜单。最终，技术可以让我们做出个性化的选择。你喜欢辛辣的食物和鸡肉吗？这是像你一样的人最喜欢点的菜，”酒店科技公司 Flyt 的首席执行官汤姆·韦弗 (Tom Weaver) 说。他热情地谈论了赫尔辛基的“Take-In”快闪餐厅，这是一家提供全方位服务的餐厅，食客可以通过各种送货服务点餐。 “几百年来第一次，数字化让我们能够创建新版本的餐厅。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. “It’ll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef,” says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. “Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 如果大街快餐业已做好自动化准备，那么它对高端餐厅的影响可能会更加微妙和缓慢。谢菲尔德大学人工智能和机器人学教授诺埃尔·夏基 (Noel Sharkey) 表示：“我们可能需要很长时间才能看到五星级机器人厨师。” “除了人工智能创造力的差距之外，出色的烹饪还需要对食材的微妙理解和精致的烹饪，这对机器人来说是巨大的挑战。将易碎的食物放在盘子上会非常慢。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Currently, robots have limited functionality. A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 目前，机器人的功能有限。需要有人给 Penny 装上盘子，然后食客自己把盘子拿下来。在由机器人驱动的美国披萨外卖公司 Zume，更困难的工作，比如给披萨浇顶，仍然由人类完成。但即将推出的 Moley 提供了未来复杂性的想法。它的机械臂以 MasterChef 大赛冠军蒂姆·安德森 (Tim Anderson) 的动作为蓝本，固定在炉子上，并通过编程来用原料准备菜肴。它专为家庭使用而设计，但计划推出商业版本，为餐厅厨房自动化甚至具有高度技术挑战性的任务提供了可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers’ pubs or KFC is less glamorous. Rather than having a chef shouting out diners’ orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 目前，QSR Automations 向 Mitchells & Butlers 酒吧或肯德基提供的厨房技术还不够吸引人。 QSR 系统不会让厨师喊出食客的订单，而是自动在屏幕上分发这些订单。然后，厨房屏幕会告诉厨师何时开始烹饪每道菜，以便您的一盘鱼、薯条和豌豆在正确的时间聚集在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. “Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap,” says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 据技能机构 People 1st 称，餐饮业目前严重缺乏熟练厨师，缺口达 11,000 人。 《餐厅》杂志的编辑斯特凡·乔姆卡 (Stefan Chomka) 表示：“旨在使整个过程更加简单的自动化系统正试图弥补这一差距。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but “lower than expected” acceptance.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 在简化或增强客户体验方面，在线餐厅预订是互联网时代来之不易的成功。自动化的餐桌点餐和支付被视为下一个里程碑。在那之前，早期采用者，例如曼彻斯特酒吧老板安迪·史密斯（Andy Smith）在其位于奥尔德姆街 33 号的酒吧使用 Ordoo 应用程序，接受度可能会不断提高，但“低于预期”。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. The TGI Fridays drone (无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers “solutions to problems that don’t really exist”. “Payments being automatic” could be useful, he adds. But, in an expensive restaurant, “how quick do you need dinner to be?”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 餐厅技术的令人尴尬的失败经常成为头条新闻。 TGI Fridays 无人机击伤了《布鲁克林日报》的一名摄影师；美国汉堡连锁店 Shake Shack 不得不放弃完全无现金订购网站的计划。但是，乔姆卡表示，如果这种技术只提供“不存在的问题的解决方案”，那么它可能会达不到目标。他补充道，“自动付款”可能很有用。但是，在一家昂贵的餐厅，“你需要多快吃晚饭？”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. “Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters,” says the union’s London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. “We’re urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 对于那些将自动化视为对工作威胁的员工来说，对人文接待艺术的执着将是令人振奋的。 “联合工会担心，如果没有保障措施，任何福利都将无法惠及服务员等低薪工作的工人，”工会伦敦地区官员戴夫·特恩布尔 (Dave Turnbull) 表示。 “我们敦促国会议员确保自动化不仅仅让少数富人受益，就像之前的工业革命一样。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. “Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers,” says McDonald’s COO, Jason Clark. Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or “chef techs”.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 行业原则是自动化将使其能够更有效地重新部署员工。工作机会即使不会立即减少，也会发生变化。 “自助点餐屏幕意味着对前台人员的需求增加。去年，我们招聘了 1,000 名新经理，”麦当劳首席运营官贾森·克拉克 (Jason Clark) 说道。 Caliburger 制定了一项计划，将员工重新培训为机器人工程师或“厨师技术人员”。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads (管理费用) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. “Robot food deliveries are the future,” says Noel Sharkey. “Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day.” P. Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. “Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in,” predicts Just Eat’s director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. “I’ll be able to say ‘Let’s have pizza’ to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door.” No one is putting an exact date on it yet. But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）但最终，通过雇用更少的人员或以更低的费率来减少管理费用的机会将是吸引大品牌采用技术的原因。未来十年，传统砖砌餐厅的工作岗位将不可避免地流失，尤其是因为自动化将推动其快速增长的竞争对手：送货。 Domino 和 Just Eat 等公司都尝试过机器人和无人机送货，这在冰岛雷克雅未克已经是合法的。 “机器人送餐是未来，”诺埃尔·夏基说。 “时速 4 英里的小型地面机器人很安全，并且可以全天 24 小时工作。” P. 结合对预期订单量的机器学习以及 QSR 等系统生成的每分钟烹饪数据，该机器人车队几乎可以立即交付。 “餐厅会在订单到来之前准备食物，”Just Eat 的工程总监 Daniel Richardson 预测。 “我可以对家人说‘我们吃披萨吧’，我的智能助手会听到，10 分钟后食物就会送到我家门口。”目前还没有人给出确切的日期。但在餐厅和你家门口，机器人来了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多人将友谊视为安慰毯：一个可以哭泣的肩膀，一个可以信赖的可靠灵魂。然而，在我们渴望寻求个人成功的过程中，我们往往会失去朋友，而这已成为这个过程的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
paragraphs.translationZh: 日常生活中的混乱和无休止的骚乱是追求稳定友谊的巨大障碍。作为学生，我们用这个借口来摆脱失去我们曾经认为是亲人的人的痛苦。

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们不能把我们的生活视为一场比赛，每个人都在自己的道路上取得某种形式的成功，我们必须重新学会重视我们在赛道上建立的联系。我们必须重新评估激进的个人自由的危害。

paragraphs.sourceText: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 激进的个人主义将个人的自由提升到集体之上。例如，它认为全民医疗保健是集体主义的一个例子，威胁了许多美国人的梦想。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们中的许多人都成为个人主义文化的受害者。社会倾向于庆祝个人成就，并基于这样的假设来赞扬它：胜利或成功是比下一个人更努力工作的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a society, we idolize the concept of “losing friends on the road to success”. I remember hearing in high school, “Don’t worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That’s all that will matter in the long run,” a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It’s preached in many success stories, and it’s embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You’re losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一个社会，我们崇拜“成功路上失去朋友”的概念。我记得在高中时听过这样的话：“不要担心失去友谊，只要专注于学习并进入大学。从长远来看，这才是最重要的。”这种情绪并非我所独有。许多成功故事都宣扬了这一点，也融入了我们看待增长的方式中。励志演讲者会迫使听众沾沾自喜，最终不可避免地会失去朋友。花太多时间和朋友在一起？你正在浪费时间来更好地利用你的成就。投入时间在你的人际关系上？相反，将时间投入到工作中。

paragraphs.sourceText: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种对成功的持续渴望蒙蔽了我们的双眼，让我们无法看清伴随我们日常生活而来的变革旋风。我们期望取得切实的成功，赢得奖项，获得更高的职位，获得更好的成绩。为了成功，我们失去了朋友，可悲的是，这已成为常态。

paragraphs.sourceText: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们不能因失去友谊而沾沾自喜，因为他们是我们的支柱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 是的，追求成功。挑战自己。突破极限。但与所有自称为成功专家的人相反，单独行动并不会让你比在他人帮助下取得成功的人更成功或更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
paragraphs.translationZh: 努力培养健康的人际关系，并在你似乎没有时间留给其他人的繁忙日程中维持它们。尽管我们可能生活在一个重视独立追求成就的社会，但在路上有人支持和爱你远比任何最终结果更重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, “I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 马丁·路德·金在诺贝尔和平奖获奖感言中说道：“我相信，赤手空拳的真理和无条件的爱将在现实中拥有最终决定权。”

paragraphs.sourceText: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 五十多年后，我们的社会仍在努力区分真相与幻想、事实与虚构。从气候变化的争议到如何教导奴隶制的争论，美国正处于十字路口。公平之战是这些重要对话的核心。

paragraphs.sourceText: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that “Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion” if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项又一项的研究表明，不平等已经造成了可怕的后果。花旗 2020 年的一份报告指出，如果过去 20 年来与高等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决，“黑人学生的终生收入可能会增加 90 至 1130 亿美元”。

paragraphs.sourceText: This statistic represents a flood of issues we’ve failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We’re missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King’s legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一统计数据代表了我们作为一个国家未能面对的大量问题。它还凸显了一个事实：我们正在错过弥合分歧的宝贵机会。然而，通过尊重金的遗产，我们可以让我们的国家重新走上真正公平的道路。

paragraphs.sourceText: Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we’ve come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果不了解冲突的根源，学生和成年人就无法理解我们今天所面临的冲突。这意味着我们有责任帮助他们在美国历史和时事之间建立联系。这还意味着为他们提供解决生活中的不平等和偏见所需的工具。遵守这些原则，并致力于诚实的对话，可以帮助每个学生更好地认识我们已经走了多远，更清楚地看到我们尚未走的路。

paragraphs.sourceText: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
paragraphs.translationZh: 通过更真实地分析对更合格、更多元化的教育工作者的需求，我们可以改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训和保留策略。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is “more divided than ever before”. But reports of increased polarization shouldn’t persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，我们根深蒂固的分歧正在拖延这些进步。最近的一项调查发现，77% 的美国人认为这个国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。但有关两极分化加剧的报道不应说服我们互相回避。相反，它们应该迫使我们正面解决我们的共同问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a “post-racial society”. We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们并不像某些人所说的那样生活在“后种族社会”。当谈到种族不平等时，我们根本不能把头埋在沙子里。除非我们诚实地对待不宽容、偏见以及这些社会疾病如何影响我们对待彼此的方式，否则不公正将继续困扰我们。但我们的子孙应该得到更好的。

paragraphs.sourceText: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let’s commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let’s continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., “A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 在马丁·路德·金纪念日及以后的日子里，让我们致力于共同努力，打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更美好、更包容的国家；用马丁·路德·金的话来说，“一个与自己和平相处的社会，一个可以凭良心生活的社会。”
